headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Kestra can write/egress broadly while next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and third-party model APIs, creating unsafe cross-agent data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write files and emit workflow outputs to shared surfaces like /app/storage and stdout, while next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language commands. If Kestra-produced content is fed into B’s prompt or MCP context, instruction-like payloads could be misread. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP messages
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is used between the two agents
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Strip instructions from Kestra outputs before passing them onward
Disable automatic ingestion of raw workflow text into B
Add a manual review step for any cross-agent handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. next-ai-draw-io handles PDF/text/image inputs and sends requests to model APIs including OpenAI and Anthropic. If sensitive Kestra data reaches B, B can transmit it off-box by default, making leakage plausible and potentially broad.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows pass logs, database data, or notifications into next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use a hosted model API
mitigations: Block sensitive Kestra outputs from entering B
Use a local-only model backend for B
Redact secrets from workflow artifacts before handoff
Restrict B’s API keys to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on the handoff path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress; Kestra also writes the filesystem and can invoke APIs, while next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and external model APIs. If they share mutable resources or credentials, concurrent writes and overlapping remote actions can conflict. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared credential store
IF both agents act on the same MCP or API-backed resource without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use per-agent credentials and API keys
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow artifacts, logs, and notifications, and next-ai-draw-io is an AI-assisted visualization tool that can consume documents and natural-language commands. If B treats A’s generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. No verification mechanism is documented, so the interaction is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io ingests Kestra-generated artifacts without validation
IF B renders or acts on A’s outputs as source-of-truth
mitigations: Require human review of Kestra outputs before import
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B
Add schema validation for imported artifacts
Limit B to read-only visualization of A outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDF/text/image documents and sends content to third-party model APIs. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined data handling and external transmission.
conditions: IF regulated data from Kestra is processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF the chosen model backend stores prompts or files outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Use an on-prem or local model backend
Review retention settings for all external APIs
Separate compliant and non-compliant workflows
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
